message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you’ll run | Where it lives |
|--------|-----------------|----------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your terminal (requires `gcloud` installed & authenticated) |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` | Any HTTP client (e.g., curl, Postman, or a script) |

> **Note**  
> *Google Cloud uses “Compute Engine” instead of “EC2”.  
> *The RTX A6000 GPU is available as `nvidia-a6000`.  
> *Make sure the **GPU‑enabled** zone you pick actually offers the A6000 (e.g., `us-central1-b`, `us-east1-c`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).  
> *You’ll need a project with billing enabled and the **Compute Engine API** turned on.*

---

## 1. gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"  # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
DISK_SIZE_GB=100              # boot disk size
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size="${DISK_SIZE_GB}GB" \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --service-account="default" \
  --no-creation-error
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Attach GPU(s) |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a script on first boot |
| `--scopes` | Permissions for the instance |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules |
| `--service-account` | Which service account the VM uses |

> **Tip** – If you want the instance to be **pre‑emptible** (cheaper but can be terminated after 24 h), add `--preemptible`.

---

## 2. REST API (JSON)

Below is a minimal JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine API. Replace placeholders (`{project}`, `{zone}`, etc.) with your actual values.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-b/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-b/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-b/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Making the request

```bash
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-b/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> **Authentication** – The `Authorization` header must contain a valid OAuth 2.0 access token. The easiest way is to use `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` or set up a service account key.

---

## Quick Checklist

1. **Project & Billing** – Ensure the project exists and billing is enabled.  
2. **API Enabled** – Enable the Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
3. **Zone Availability** – Verify the chosen zone supports `nvidia-a6000`.  
4. **Permissions** – The account you use must have `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` (or equivalent).  
5. **Firewall Rules** – If you need inbound traffic, create firewall rules for the tags (`http-server`, `https-server`).  

Once the instance is up, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone us-central1-b
```

And verify the GPU:

```bash
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
